question:
For real parameters $k$ and $\lambda$, consider
$$x+y=2$$
$$2x+ky=\lambda$$

(a) Determine the condition on $k$ for which the system has a unique solution and obtain that solution.

(b) When $k=2$, determine the value of $\lambda$ for which the system has infinitely many solutions.

(c) State the condition on $\lambda$ for which the system is inconsistent when $k=2$.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient determinant is
$$D= egin{vmatrix}1 & 1\2 & k\end{vmatrix}=k-2$$
The system has a unique solution when
$$k eq2$$
From $x+y=2$,
$$x=2-y$$
Substituting in the second equation,
$$2(2-y)+ky=\lambda$$
$$4+(k-2)y=\lambda$$
Therefore,
$$y= rac{\lambda-4}{k-2}$$
and
$$x=2- rac{\lambda-4}{k-2}= rac{2k-\lambda}{k-2}$$

(b)
When $k=2$, the equations become
$$x+y=2$$
$$2x+2y=\lambda$$
Twice the first equation is $2x+2y=4$. Therefore, the two equations are identical when
$$\lambda=4$$
In this case, the system has infinitely many solutions.

(c)
When $k=2$ and $\lambda eq4$, the left-hand side of the second equation is twice that of the first equation, but its right-hand side is not twice the first right-hand side. Therefore, the system is inconsistent for
$$\lambda eq4$$

options.A:
(a) Unique solution for $k\neq2$: $x=\frac{\lambda-2k}{k-2},\ y=\frac{4-\lambda}{k-2}$
(b) For $k=2$, infinitely many solutions when $\lambda=-4$
(c) Inconsistent when $\lambda\neq-4$
options.B:
(a) Unique solution only for $k=2$
(b) Infinitely many solutions for every $\lambda$
(c) The system is never inconsistent
options.C:
(a) Unique solution for $k\neq0$: $x=\frac{2k-\lambda}{k},\ y=\frac{\lambda-4}{k}$
(b) For $k=2$, infinitely many solutions when $\lambda=2$
(c) Inconsistent when $\lambda\neq2$
options.D:
(a) Unique solution for $k\neq2$: $x=\frac{2k-\lambda}{k-2},\ y=\frac{\lambda-4}{k-2}$
(b) For $k=2$, infinitely many solutions when $\lambda=4$
(c) For $k=2$, the system is inconsistent when $\lambda\neq4$
